arxiv-2202-02474.title: Importance Weighting Approach in Kernel Bayes’ Rule
arxiv-2202-02474.creator: Liyuan Xu, Yutian Chen, Arnaud Doucet, Arthur Gretton
arxiv-2202-02474.description: Abstract We study a nonparametric approach to Bayesian computation via feature means, where the expectation of prior features is updated to yield expected kernel posterior features, based on regression from learned neural net or kernel features of the observations. All quantities involved in the Bayesian update are learned from observed data, making the method entirely model-free.

arxiv-2210-02383.title: Filling the Gaps: A Multiple Imputation Approach to Estimating Aging Curves in Baseball
arxiv-2210-02383.creator: Quang Nguyen, Gregory J. Matthews
arxiv-2210-02383.description: Abstract In sports, an aging curve depicts the relationship between average performance and age in athletes’ careers. This paper investigates the aging curves for offensive players in Major League Baseball. We study this problem in a missing data context and account for different types of dropouts of baseball players during their careers.

arxiv-2211-03855.title: The ZX-calculus as a Language for Topological Quantum Computation
arxiv-2211-03855.creator: Fatimah Rita Ahmadi, Aleks Kissinger
arxiv-2211-03855.description: Abstract Unitary fusion categories formalise the algebraic theory of topological quantum computation. These categories come naturally enriched in a subcategory of the category of Hilbert spaces, and by looking at this subcategory, one can identify a collection of generators for implementing quantum computation.

arxiv-2211-11377.title: Lifespan estimates for the compressible Euler equations with damping via Orlicz spaces techniques
arxiv-2211-11377.creator: Ning-An Lai, Nico Michele Schiavone
arxiv-2211-11377.description: Abstract In this paper we are interested in the upper bound of the lifespan estimate for the compressible Euler system with time dependent damping and small initial perturbations. We employ some techniques from the blow-up study of nonlinear wave equations.

arxiv-2403-05577.title: Stress Monitoring Using Low-Cost Electroencephalogram Devices: A Systematic Literature Review Journal: International Journal of Medical Informatics
arxiv-2403-05577.creator: Gideon Vos, Maryam Ebrahimpour, Liza van Eijk, Zoltan Sarnyai, Mostafa Rahimi Azghadi
arxiv-2403-05577.description: Abstract Introduction Low-cost, consumer grade wearable health monitoring devices are increasingly being used for mental health related studies including stress. While cortisol response magnitude remains the gold standard indicator for stress assessment, a growing number of studies have started to use low-cost EEG devices and wrist-based wearable device monitors as primary recorders of biomarker data.

arxiv-2406-18646.title: Using 3.4- 𝝁 \bm{\mu} m Variability towards White Dwarfs as a Signpost of Remnant Planetary Systems Facilities: WISE, NEOWISE, Gaia, LDT, SOAR, TESS, ASAS-SN

arxiv-2406-18646.description: Abstract Roughly 2% of white dwarfs harbor planetary debris disks detectable via infrared excesses, but only a few percent of these disks show a gaseous component, distinguished by their double-peaked emission at the near-infrared calcium triplet. Previous studies found most debris disks around white dwarfs are variable at 3.4 and 4.

arxiv-2410-22196.title: LLL Algorithm for Lattice Basis Reduction
arxiv-2410-22196.creator: Alex Kalbach, Ted Chinburg
arxiv-2410-22196.description: Abstract This is an expository paper intended to introduce the polynomial time lattice basis reduction algorithm first described by Arjen Lenstra, Hendrik Lenstra, and László Lovász in 1982. We begin by introducing the shortest vector problem, which motivates the underlying components of the LLL algorithm.

arxiv-2501-16138.title: Quantifying the Self-Interest Level of Markov Social Dilemmas
arxiv-2501-16138.creator: Richard Willis, Yali Du, Joel Z Leibo, Michael Luck
arxiv-2501-16138.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel method for estimating the self-interest level of Markov social dilemmas. We extend the concept of self-interest level from normal-form games to Markov games, providing a quantitative measure of the minimum reward exchange required to align individual and collective interests.

arxiv-2506-09476.title: Urban1960SatSeg: Unsupervised Semantic Segmentation of Mid-20 th century Urban Landscapes with Satellite Imageries CCS: Computing methodologies Image segmentation
arxiv-2506-09476.creator: Tianxiang Hao, Lixian Zhang, Yingjia Zhang, Mengxuan Chen, Jinxiao Zhang, Haohuan Fu
arxiv-2506-09476.description: Abstract . Historical satellite imagery, such as mid-20 th century Keyhole data, offers rare insights into understanding early urban development and long-term transformation. However, severe quality degradation ( e.g. , distortion, misalignment, and spectral scarcity) and annotation absence have long hindered semantic segmentation on such historical RS imagery.

arxiv-2506-12469.title: Levels of Autonomy for AI Agents Working Paper
arxiv-2506-12469.creator: K. J. Kevin Feng David W. McDonald Amy X. Zhang University of Washington kjfeng@uw.edu
arxiv-2506-12469.description: Abstract Autonomy is a double-edged sword for AI agents, simultaneously unlocking transformative possibilities and serious risks. How can agent developers calibrate the appropriate levels of autonomy at which their agents should operate? We argue that an agent’s level of autonomy can be treated as a deliberate design decision, separate from its capability and operational environment.

pmc-11432542.title: Laparoscopic Fertility-Sparing Management of Borderline Ovarian Tumors: Surgical and Long-Term Oncological Outcomes
pmc-11432542.creator: Marta Tortajada Valle, Núria Agustí, Pere Fusté, Eduard Mensión, Berta Díaz-Feijóo, Ariel Glickman, Tiermes Marina, Aureli Torné
pmc-11432542.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objectives: To assess the long-term oncological safety of laparoscopic fertility-sparing surgery (FSS) in borderline ovarian tumors and the impact of laparoscopic surgical factors on recurrences. Primary outcomes were the recurrence rate and time to recurrence after laparoscopic FSS. Secondary outcomes were to evaluate the recurrence rate after a second laparoscopic surgery and to assess factors associated with the risk of relapse. Methods: This is a retrospective single-center observational study in a tertiary university-affiliated hospital.

pmc-11475950.title: BUB1 Inhibition Overcomes Radio- and Chemoradiation Resistance in Lung Cancer
pmc-11475950.creator: Shivani Thoidingjam, Sushmitha Sriramulu, Oudai Hassan, Stephen L. Brown, Farzan Siddiqui, Benjamin Movsas, Shirish Gadgeel, Shyam Nyati
pmc-11475950.description: Simple SummaryElevated levels of the mitotic checkpoint kinase BUB1 are frequently observed in most solid cancers, including lung cancer. High BUB1 expression is linked to poorer patient survival. In the present study, we aimed to evaluate if a BUB1 targeting agent could enhance the effectiveness of chemotherapy and chemoradiation in lung cancer.

pmc-13074995.title: Influence of Prosthetic Substrate, Cement, and Opaquer Liner on Color Matching of Translucent Zirconia- and Lithium-Based Ceramics
pmc-13074995.creator: Beata Dejak, Bartłomiej Konieczny, Agata Szczesio-Wlodarczyk, Wioleta Stopa
pmc-13074995.description: Highlights Optical properties of translucent zirconia- and lithium-based ceramics were evaluated.The translucency of the tested ceramics was as follows: LDS >> ZLS > zirconia ceramics.The use of an opaque liner reduced the translucency of the ceramics but did not mask the metal substrate.Transparent or colored luting material on tooth abutments provided the most favorable shade matching.

pmc-13322009.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and RNAi screening define a hierarchical program of planarian eye regeneration
pmc-13322009.creator: M Lucila Scimone, Bryanna I Canales, Patrick Aoude, Kutay D Atabay, Cyrille W Teforlack, Peter W Reddien
pmc-13322009.description: SUMMARYThe evolution and development of eyes are fundamental problems in biology, and numerous genetic and age-related degenerative eye diseases are still poorly understood. Planarians are flatworms that are able to fully regenerate functional eyes following injury, presenting a powerful model to study essential attributes of eye biology and regeneration.

pmc-13463494.title: Integrated multi-omics profiling uncovers the epigenetic, transcriptional, and metabolic landscape of prostate cancer progression
pmc-13463494.creator: Christine Aaserød Pedersen, Maximilian Wess, Maria K Andersen, Elise Midtbust, Abhibhav Sharma, Thomas Fleischer, Morten Beck Rye, May-Britt Tessem
pmc-13463494.description: A comprehensive understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms of prostate cancer is essential for the development of precise diagnostic biomarkers. In this study, we applied the unsupervised multi-omics factor analysis framework (MOFA) to integrate DNA methylation, gene expression, and metabolic profiles derived from the same individuals, aiming to characterize the biological landscape of normal, malignant, and aggressive prostate tissue.

pmc-13556347.title: Retinoic acid is a translation inhibitor against chikungunya virus both in vitro and invivo
pmc-13556347.creator: Yibo Chen, Zhiwei He, Ke Zhang, Xijing Qian, Yangang Liu, Xu Zheng, Ping Zhao, Zhongtian Qi, Cuiling Ding
pmc-13556347.description: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a mosquito-borne alphavirus, causes debilitating febrile and arthritic disease and remains a persistent public health threat in tropical and subtropical regions, with no clinically approved antiviral drugs currently available, which underscores the urgent need for targeted and effective therapeutic interventions.

pmc-13606677.title: Gellan Gum Modification and Structural Regulation for Food Applications: Delivery Systems and Digestive Behavior
pmc-13606677.creator: Yong Zhou, Shiyi Chen, Yan Jiang, Afira Nayab, Ling Sun
pmc-13606677.description: Gellan gum (GG) is an anionic microbial polysaccharide widely used in foods because of its efficient gelation, thermal stability, and ion-responsive structuring. However, the contrasting limitations of high- and low-acyl GG, together with their sensitivity to molecular weight, ions, pH, thermal history, and food-matrix composition, restrict their performance in complex products.
